:::{#def-lagrangian}
#### Lagrangian

For the problem of minimizing $f(\vx)$ over $\vx \in \reals^p$ subject to $\tp{\matr{A}} \vx = \vecf{b}$,
with $\matr{A}$ a $p \times m$ matrix and $\vecf{b} \in \reals^m$,
the **Lagrangian** is the function of $\vx \in \reals^p$ and $\vecf{\lambda} \in \reals^m$

$$
L(\vx, \vecf{\lambda}) \eqdef f(\vx) + \tp{\vecf{\lambda}} \paren{\tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \vecf{b}},
$$

and the entries of $\vecf{\lambda}$ are the **Lagrange multipliers**, one per constraint.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-lagrangian}
#### The gradients of the Lagrangian of a quadratic

Let $f(\vx) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vx} \matr{S} \vx$ with $\matr{S}$ symmetric and constant.
The constraint term is a dot product in two ways:

$$
\ba
\tp{\vecf{\lambda}} \paren{\tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \vecf{b}}
&= \tp{\vecf{\lambda}} \tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \tp{\vecf{\lambda}} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\
&= (\matr{A} \vecf{\lambda}) \cdot \vx - \tp{\vecf{\lambda}} \vecf{b},
&& \text{(transpose of a product; dot product)}
\ea
$$

and it equals $\paren{\tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \vecf{b}} \cdot \vecf{\lambda}$ directly.
The [transpose of a product](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-transpose-product) gives $\tp{\vecf{\lambda}} \tp{\matr{A}} = \tp{(\matr{A} \vecf{\lambda})}$.
Differentiating each term, with partial derivatives adding term by term,

$$
\ba
\deriv{\vx} L(\vx, \vecf{\lambda})
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \matr{S} \vx + \matr{A} \vecf{\lambda} - \vzero_{p \times 1}
&& \text{(@thm-quadratic-form; @thm-deriv-lincom; } \tp{\vecf{\lambda}} \vecf{b} \text{ is constant in } \vx \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{S} \vx + \matr{A} \vecf{\lambda},
&& \text{(simplify)}
\\
\deriv{\vecf{\lambda}} L(\vx, \vecf{\lambda})
&= \vzero_{m \times 1} + \paren{\tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \vecf{b}}
&& \text{(} f(\vx) \text{ is constant in } \vecf{\lambda} \text{; @thm-deriv-lincom)}
\\
&= \tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \vecf{b}.
&& \text{(simplify)}
\ea
$$

So $(\vx, \vecf{\lambda})$ makes both gradients $\vzero$ exactly when

$$
\matr{S} \vx + \matr{A} \vecf{\lambda} = \vzero_{p \times 1}
\quad \text{and} \quad
\tp{\matr{A}} \vx = \vecf{b},
\qquad\text{that is,}\qquad
\underbrace{\sbmat{ \matr{S} & \matr{A} \\ \tp{\matr{A}} & \vzero_{m \times m} }}_{(p + m) \times (p + m)}
\underbrace{\sbmat{ \vx \\ \vecf{\lambda} }}_{(p + m) \times 1}
= \underbrace{\sbmat{ \vzero_{p \times 1} \\ \vecf{b} }}_{(p + m) \times 1},
$$ {#eq-kkt}

the second equation being the constraint itself.
The block matrix is the **saddle point matrix** (or KKT matrix) of the problem.

:::
